title: IARPA request to study CRISPR-Cas9 DNA data encoding
summary: Bob Maguire tells of IARPA request to study CRISPR-Cas9 DNA data encoding, about 2013-2014 at IARPA; Hume Center, Virginia Tech, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: the current deputy director dni Stacy Dixon was the director when I was asked could I take a look at using CRA crisper cast 9 encoding information into DNA

plain: Bob Maguire, who describes himself as a contractor for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, told podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2013 or 2014 he was asked to look into storing information inside DNA using CRISPR-Cas9, a tool for editing genes. He says the request came through IARPA, a US government agency that funds research for the intelligence services, and his work was tied to the Hume Center, a research center at Virginia Tech university. He says it happened when Stacy Dixon, later deputy to the Director of National Intelligence (the head of all US spy agencies), was running IARPA, which would suggest the intelligence world was quietly exploring DNA as a way to hold data.
